purpose: Bind an immutable task publication generation to the currently winning authorized Issue #240 owner claim. Ordinary work binds the operational publication at task scope; an opt-in execution cohort binds one retained publication at exact task+cohort+lane scope. Both paths preserve Researcher-ID, theorem-owner classification, execution branch/base, output scope and owner lease without turning GitHub persistence into the research hot path.

claim_envelope_normalization.researcher_id: If absent, derive deterministically from task_id plus claim_id using the existing identity lane.
claim_envelope_normalization.taskbook_blob_sha1: Resolved from the exact immutable publication record selected by the ordinary operational route or execution lane; callers do not need to duplicate it.
claim_envelope_normalization.lease_minutes: If absent, inherit the task claim lease.
claim_envelope_normalization.execution_scope: execution_cohort_id and execution_lane_id are both present or both absent; active cohorts require both.

runtime_authorization_gate.event_evidence: One local export of the existing raw Issue #240 comments at the execution/adoption semantic boundary; canonical dispatch normalizes server metadata, actor authorization, claim-envelope validation and lease reduction locally.

parallel_execution.lane_publication: exact publication_id pinned by the lane; it may be retained and non-operational
parallel_execution.lane_output_scope: every allowed output path/prefix must stay under lane.output_prefix

persistence_boundary.claim: One Issue #240 CLAIM per owner scope is sufficient to begin registered execution after canonical validation; do not require a prior commit, PR, merge, CI wait, heartbeat, or second GitHub write.
persistence_boundary.execution_authorization_read: At execution start or stale adoption, consume one current Issue #240 raw comment export and reduce it locally; do not turn this into periodic polling between semantic checkpoints.
persistence_boundary.execution_record: The immutable execution record is durable provenance for result freezing. It may be created locally after CLAIM and batched with the first genuine durable checkpoint or final return; it is not a pre-math remote publication gate.
persistence_boundary.parallel_cohort: One immutable cohort record defines the lanes. Each lane then uses the same ordinary one-CLAIM boundary; there is no extra heartbeat or synchronization write between semantic checkpoints.
persistence_boundary.between_checkpoints: Zero routine repository writes, zero CI polling, zero review polling and zero scheduler heartbeat are required solely by this contract.

distributed_transaction.noncohort: Validate operational task publication -> create/verify execution branch -> append one self-contained authorized CLAIM envelope on Issue #240 -> first valid live task-scope CLAIM wins -> runtime guard reconstructs that same winner -> research -> freeze execution provenance only when a genuine durable checkpoint/result requires it.
distributed_transaction.cohort: Freeze cohort with disjoint lanes -> each lane validates its pinned retained publication and branch/output namespace -> append one authorized lane CLAIM -> first valid live CLAIM wins that exact lane -> sibling lanes may proceed concurrently -> each lane freezes its own durable provenance/result -> exact cohort evidence proceeds to two reference passes and synthesis.

compatibility: Previously frozen non-cohort execution records and their IDs remain readable with unchanged semantics. A historical execution intent may still supply the binding for its matching live CLAIM, but it does not replace the requirement that the current Issue #240 claim wins the relevant task/lane owner race.
